items.title: Google Tested AI Headlines In Discover. Now It's Testing Them In Search
items.summary: Google has begun testing AI-generated headline rewrites in traditional search results, following a similar experiment in Discover that quickly became a feature. The test uses generative AI to create new headlines matching user queries more effectively, affecting various sites without disclosure. This shift reduces publishers' control over branding and could challenge SEO strategies reliant on original titles.

items.title: 5 GEO Strategies To Make AI Search Recommend Your Brand In 2026
items.summary: Brands can boost AI visibility by tracking mentions in tools like ChatGPT and Perplexity, building on strong SEO with citability-focused content using clear claims, schema, and topical authority. Engaging in Reddit discussions and listicles on trusted sites increases citation chances. SEO now serves as a foundation for GEO, prioritizing authoritative, structured content over keywords amid rising AI dominance.

items.title: 93% of AI Search Sessions End Without Website Visits – Shift to GEO and AEO
items.summary: Traditional SEO is obsolete as 93% of AI searches yield no clicks, with AI Overviews in 25% of queries and citation confidence replacing page rank. Marketers must structure content for AI trust in under 40-word blocks, as traditional search drops 25% yearly. Early AI citation tracking tools like Semrush position brands to dominate discovery.

items.title: Open-Source geo-seo-claude Tool Audits Sites for AI Citation Readiness
items.summary: AI search is eroding Google traffic, leaving most sites invisible to ChatGPT and Perplexity; geo-seo-claude audits URLs for GEO readiness, crawler access, and generates PDF reports. AI-referred traffic converts 4.4x higher than organic, yet traditional SEO lags. Fully open-source under MIT, empowering quick AI optimization.

items.title: Generative Engine Optimization (GEO): Key Tactics for AI Citation in 2026
items.summary: GEO optimizes content for citation in AI responses from ChatGPT, Perplexity, etc., differing from SEO rankings and AEO snippets by focusing on extractable, trustworthy chunks. Use modular blocks, upfront answers, schema, and question headings to ensure AI pulls and credits your content. Builds durable authority as users skip sites for direct AI answers.

items.title: Hachette Cancels 'Shy Girl' Release Over AI Allegations
items.summary: Hachette Book Group pulled the horror novel 'Shy Girl' by Mia Ballard from its schedule following allegations of AI-generated content. The book had been a self-published success before acquiring a traditional publishing deal. The author denies personal use of AI, blaming an editor, amid widespread industry scrutiny.

items.title: UK Book Trade Welcomes Axed AI Copyright Exemption
items.summary: Book publishing trade bodies applaud the UK government's decision to scrap a proposed AI copyright exception, enabling rights holders to opt out of AI training on their works. They caution that other avenues for unauthorized use persist. This development addresses growing concerns over AI's impact on creators.

items.title: Rebecca Yarros Ignites BookTok with Massive Success
items.summary: Rebecca Yarros has set BookTok ablaze, driving huge sales and discussions in the publishing world. Debates arise over authors engaging with the platform and industry implications. Her rise exemplifies BookTok's influence on book marketing and releases.

items.title: PopCrave Shares 'Shy Girl' Author Statement Post-Cancellation
items.summary: PopCrave posted the statement from 'Shy Girl' author Mia Ballard after Hachette withdrew the book due to AI writing allegations. She describes severe mental health impacts and claims innocence in AI use. The post garnered massive engagement, fueling online debate.

items.title: Jezebel on AI Infiltrating Traditional Book Publishing
items.summary: Jezebel highlights how traditional publishers are confronting AI's presence, questioning the prevalence of AI-generated novels like the canceled 'Shy Girl' by Hachette. The post links to an article on the controversy involving plagiarism concerns and slop writing. It tags key elements of the scandal.

items.title: BookTok's Impact on Book Marketing for Women
items.summary: Mac McCollum argues that BookTok has harmed book marketing towards women by prioritizing dramatic, catchy titles over straightforward ones. Marketing executives believe evocative titles are necessary to attract readers. This reflects shifts in publishing strategies driven by social media trends.

items.title: Anna Camp on Her Big ‘Scream 7’ Reveal — and Why She Apologized for That Anti-Boycott Post
items.summary: In Scream 7, Anna Camp plays Jessica Bowden, revealed as one of three Ghostface killers motivated by an abusive marriage and obsession to perfect Sidney Prescott. Camp discusses her performance clues and hopes audiences appreciate her role despite the confusing motive. She faced backlash for a social media post celebrating the failure of boycotts related to Melissa Barrera's firing over Israel-Hamas comments and issued an apology clarifying her intent to thank fans.

items.title: John Lithgow Says He Almost Backed Out of Playing Dumbledore in HBO’s ‘Harry Potter’ Over J.K. Rowling Backlash
items.summary: John Lithgow nearly withdrew from playing Albus Dumbledore in HBO's Harry Potter reboot due to intense backlash against J.K. Rowling's anti-trans views, including fan boycott threats on social media. Despite never meeting Rowling and praising her books for opposing intolerance, Lithgow felt stung by the reactions. The controversy persists, highlighted by a trans actor's discomfort and Rowling's recent criticism of Emma Watson.

items.title: David Spade Slams Gavin Newsom and Karen Bass Over 'Terrifying' Hollywood Downfall
items.summary: David Spade blamed California Governor Gavin Newsom and Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass for the decline of Hollywood's industry following the bankruptcy of another major studio lot. The comedian described the situation in LA as 'terrifying' and thanked the leaders sarcastically. The post sparked discussions on political leadership, woke content, and industry exodus.

items.title: ENHYPEN Fans Furious Over BELIFT Including Heeseung in Sales Promotions After Removing Him from Group Content
items.summary: Fans expressed outrage at BELIFT LAB for featuring Heeseung in ENHYPEN's sales promotions while excluding him from group content and activities. Accusations of exploiting the OT7 concept for profit surfaced amid demands for transparency and the member's full return. Hashtags like #ENHYPEN_IS_7 and #LET_HEESEUNG_DO_BOTH trended with fans holding the agency accountable.

items.title: David Spade Calls Out California Leaders for 'Dying' Hollywood Industry
items.summary: Fox News highlighted David Spade's criticism of Democratic leaders Karen Bass and Gavin Newsom for Hollywood's decline after a major studio bankruptcy. Spade posted 'Terrifying in LA. Thanks, Karen Bass. Thanks, Gavin.' Replies attributed the issues to woke propaganda, DEI practices, and failed policies.

items.title: SHINee's Taemin Becomes First K-Pop Soloist to Feature at Grammy Museum Alongside Michael Jackson
items.summary: SHINee's Taemin achieved a milestone as the first K-pop solo artist featured at the Grammy Museum, placed alongside pop icon Michael Jackson. The exhibit recognizes his contributions to music. Fans celebrated the global recognition for K-pop talent.

items.title: Survey: Small Businesses Embrace AI But Need Training and Support to Fully Harness It
items.summary: Small businesses across the country are rapidly adopting Artificial Intelligence (AI) and already seeing meaningful benefits, but most remain in early stages of implementation. Only 14% report AI fully embedded in core operations, while 73% indicate they would benefit from additional training and resources to maximize its potential. This highlights the growing enthusiasm for AI among SMBs alongside persistent barriers to deeper integration.<grok:render type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">12</argument></grok:render><grok:render type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">15</argument></grok:render>

items.summary: SMF Works summarizes key developments: AI agents now negotiate deals autonomously while owners sleep, a 76% vs. 14% adoption gap shows most SMBs use AI superficially, NVIDIA reports measurable revenue growth from AI, UK mandates AI content labels, and OpenAI's government deal sets compliance precedents.
